independence_day.intro: Greek Independence Day on 25 March commemorates the struggle for independence from Ottoman rule that began in 1821. The date also coincides with the Orthodox feast of the Annunciation.
independence_day.history: The Greek War of Independence began in 1821 and continued for years before an independent Greek state was recognised in 1830. The national anniversary links this historical struggle with 25 March, a significant religious date, rather than marking the completion of independence on a single day.
independence_day.traditions: School parades, flag displays, church services and official ceremonies mark the holiday. A military parade is held in Athens. Salt cod with skordalia, a garlic accompaniment, is a traditional meal associated with the Annunciation.
funFacts: The Greek flag’s blue and white colours are prominent in the celebrations.
25 March is both a national and a religious occasion.
Ochi Day on 28 October recalls a different period of Greek history.

ochi_day.intro: Ochi Day on 28 October commemorates Greece’s rejection of an Italian ultimatum in 1940 and its entry into the Second World War. The name means No Day.
ochi_day.history: On 28 October 1940, Italy demanded permission to occupy strategic positions in Greece. The Greek government rejected the ultimatum, and Italian forces invaded from Albania. The word ochi, meaning no, became a symbol of the refusal and subsequent resistance.
ochi_day.traditions: Schools and communities organise parades, flags decorate streets, and wreaths are laid at memorials. Thessaloniki hosts a major military parade. Commemorations honour those who resisted invasion and remember the suffering caused by the war.
funFacts: Ochi is also written Oxi when transliterated from Greek.
The popular name summarises the rejection rather than reproducing a formal diplomatic reply.
The holiday falls on 28 October every year.
